ruleSets.title: Texas Foundation High School Program
ruleSets.plainSummary: Texas students graduate under the Foundation High School Program: at least 22 credits in set subjects, end-of-course exams and a few forms. Most students also earn an endorsement (26 credits). Students who started 9th grade in 2026-27 or later take personal financial literacy as part of social studies.

of.label: English III (or AP or IB English)
A 4th English credit
of.note: English IV, or a listed class such as creative writing, humanities or AP English. Only the level III speech, debate and journalism classes are on the list, and Communication Applications counts only as a half credit paired with a different listed class, so ask your counselor before using one of those.

of.label: A 3rd math credit
of.note: Algebra II, precalculus, statistics or another listed class, or an applied class such as Mathematical Models with Applications. Applied classes count here but not as the 4th math for an endorsement or the Distinguished Level of Achievement.

of.label: Economics (or personal financial literacy and economics)
Two levels of the same language
AP Computer Science A (also a math credit) plus one more programming credit
AP Computer Science A or IB Computer Science HL

requirements.label: Physical education
requirements.note: By district policy, athletics, JROTC, marching band, drill team or cheerleading can earn this credit.

conditions.label: Pass the state end-of-course exams in Algebra I, Biology, English I and U.S. History
Submit a FAFSA or TASFA in 12th grade (or an opt-out form)
Choose whether the state may share your records for direct college admission
Show speaking and listening skills, in 8th grade or later

warnings.text: Physics and Physics for Engineering can't both count toward your science credits.
AP Computer Science A (or IB Computer Science HL) counts as both a math credit and a language credit. Ask your counselor how your school records it.
Dual credit classes that go beyond the matching high school class can meet graduation and endorsement requirements.
A class required for graduation only has to be taught once every two school years, so check when your school offers each one.

An 11th or 12th grader who hasn't passed up to two end-of-course exams may still graduate through an individual graduation committee. Students in special education can also graduate by completing their IEP.
You name the endorsement you plan to earn when you start 9th grade, and you can switch at any time.

Some districts require more than 22 credits. Ask your counselor for your district's total.
